chapters.title: 10.1 Tags, Grep Plugin, Conditional Test Running
chapters.overviewText: Cypress does not ship first-party test tags. The ecosystem standard is the grep plugin (@cypress/grep, historically cypress-grep): you annotate it('...', { tags: ['@smoke'] }) and select with CYPRESS_grepTags or --env grepTags= at run time. That is how you run smoke on PR, @payroll nightly, and @flake never on the merge gate. Playwright has grep/grepInvert in config; Selenium/Java uses JUnit categories or TestNG groups.
chapters.why: A 40-minute suite that cannot run a 4-minute smoke set will be skipped by developers. Tags are how Bizlevate keeps the PR gate honest without deleting coverage.
chapters.when: When CI time hurts, when you quarantine flake (9.13), and when you need @smoke vs @regression vs @okta without splitting repos.

practical.scenario: PRs must run a fast smoke set (login, leave submit, dashboard). Nightly runs everything except @flake. You must not maintain two copy-paste spec trees.
practical.pass: You install @cypress/grep, register it in e2e.ts and setupNodeEvents, tag tests, and invoke CYPRESS_grepTags=@smoke on the PR job.
practical.fail: You wrap tests in if (Cypress.env('SMOKE')) it(...) inside the spec, or you comment out tests before each release.

chapters.customSummary:
- No built-in tags — use @cypress/grep (grep plugin), not ad-hoc if (env).
- Tag it/describe via { tags: ['@smoke'] }; filter with grepTags / grep / grepInvert.
- Register the plugin in support + setupNodeEvents or tags are ignored.
- Playwright: config grep. Selenium: groups/categories. Same idea, different knob.
- Conditional running of *commands* based on DOM (if $el.length) is still an anti-pattern (12.2).

chapters.title: 10.2 Environment Variables & Multiple Environments
chapters.overviewText: Cypress.env is the in-test key/value bag. Values arrive from cypress.config env, cypress.env.json (gitignored secrets), CYPRESS_* OS variables, and --env on the CLI — later sources override earlier ones in documented order. baseUrl plus env.apiUrl let the same spec hit staging vs local. Playwright uses projects + process.env; Selenium uses properties/system env. Do not hardcode https://staging.bizlevate.com in specs.
chapters.why: HRM always has local, staging, and sometimes a prod-read-only smoke. Baking staging URLs into cy.visit is how suites pass at home and attack the wrong host in CI.
chapters.when: First time you add a second deployment, when putting passwords in git, and when GitHub Actions must inject CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY without printing it.

practical.scenario: The same leave spec must run against localhost:3000 (dev) and https://staging.bizlevate.com (CI) with different API hosts and a secret test user.
practical.pass: You set baseUrl per env, put secrets in CYPRESS_ or cypress.env.json (ignored), read Cypress.env('apiUrl') in the spec, and never commit real passwords.
practical.fail: You cy.visit('https://staging.bizlevate.com/leave') with a password string in the repo.

chapters.customSummary:
- Cypress.env('KEY') reads merged config: config.env < cypress.env.json < CYPRESS_KEY < --env.
- CYPRESS_ prefix maps OS env automatically (CYPRESS_grepTags, CYPRESS_apiUrl).
- baseUrl is config, not env — still override with CYPRESS_BASE_URL / --config baseUrl=.
- cypress.env.json is for local secrets; gitignore it. CI uses Actions secrets.
- Playwright projects vs Cypress: one config, many env files or CLI overrides — not browser projects.

chapters.title: 10.3 Retries
chapters.overviewText: Cypress can retry a whole failed test in runMode (CI) and/or openMode (the App). retries: { runMode: 2 } means up to three attempts. A pass on attempt two is a green spec and a hidden flake (9.13). Playwright Test retries and pytest-rerunfailures work the same way. Use retries as a shock absorber while you fix isolation — not as the quality strategy.
chapters.why: Teams set runMode: 4 to make GitHub green. That trains everyone to ignore the first failure. Interviewers want you to know the config *and* the moral hazard.
chapters.when: When enabling CI for the first time, when Cloud reports flake, and when you are asked to 'just turn on retries' after a flaky payroll spec.

practical.scenario: CI is noisy on leave-approve. Someone proposes retries: 5. You must configure something safer and keep flake visible.
practical.pass: You set a small runMode (1–2) if needed, leave openMode 0 so local failures stay loud, and you still ticket any test that used a retry.
practical.fail: You set retries: 5 globally and call the suite stable.

chapters.customSummary:
- retries.runMode vs openMode — CI vs App; a retry-pass is still flake.
- Whole test retries; this is not the same as command retry-ability (Part 2).
- Default is 0. Cypress 13+ keeps that unless you set it.
- Playwright retries in config; Selenium TestNG retry analyzers — same trap.
- Pair with grep @flake quarantine (10.1) rather than infinite retries.
chapters.contentMarkdown:
## Two different "retries"

**Command retry-ability** (Part 2): `cy.get('.row').should('have.length', 3)` re-queries until timeout. That is Cypress's core waiting model. It is good.

**Test retries:** if the `it()` fails, Mocha/Cypress runs the entire test again.

```js
// cypress.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  retries: { runMode: 1, openMode: 0 },
});

// per-test override
it('payroll csv export', { retries: 2 }, () => { /* ... */ });
```

`runMode: 1` ⇒ original + one retry (two attempts). `openMode: 0` ⇒ when you watch in the App, a fail stays a fail so you debug it.

## Why retries hide flake

Attempt 1: approve button covered by a toast. Fail. Attempt 2: toast gone. Pass. CI is green. The toast still races. Cloud (11.3) can mark this flaky *if you record*. Without Cloud, look for "Attempt 2 of 2" in the log and treat it as a defect.

## Policy for Bizlevate

- Default global retries **0** until the suite is honest.
- If CI hardware is bursty, `runMode: 1` max as a shock absorber.
- Never retry `@okta` 5 times to paper over a bad `cy.origin` (9.1).
- Quarantine with `@flake` + grepInvert on PR (10.1, 9.13).

## Versus Playwright and Selenium

Playwright: `retries: 2` in `playwright.config`. pytest-rerunfailures: `--reruns 2`. TestNG: `IRetryAnalyzer`. All of them can make a dashboard look healthy. Senior engineers report retry rate as a KPI.

Interview line: "Command retries are waiting. Test retries hide flake. I keep `openMode` at 0 and I never use retries as the fix."

chapters.title: 10.4 Headless vs Headed Runs, Viewport/Device Testing
chapters.overviewText: cypress open is headed and interactive. cypress run is headless by default (no GUI, suitable for CI) and can be --headed. Viewport comes from config viewportWidth/Height, cy.viewport(), or presets like iphone-x — it resizes the app iframe, it does not start iOS. Pair with 9.9/9.17: Chrome headless is not Safari, and a phone preset is not a device lab.
chapters.why: People debug in open mode at 1500px then CI fails at the default 1280×720, or they think --headed on Actions gives them the Cypress App. Those are different surfaces.
chapters.when: Writing the first CI job, reproducing a CI-only layout bug, and adding a mobile-width spec.

practical.scenario: Dashboard cards wrap in CI but not on your laptop. You need a headed local run at the CI viewport, then a mobile-width check for the leave form.
practical.pass: You match viewportWidth/Height to CI, reproduce with cypress run --headed, and add cy.viewport('iphone-x') only for responsive specs — without claiming native mobile.
practical.fail: You only use cypress open at fullscreen and you set headed: true in CI expecting the App UI Mode.

chapters.customSummary:
- cypress open = App GUI. cypress run = CI runner; default headless; --headed is still not the App.
- Pin viewportWidth/Height in config so local run matches CI.
- cy.viewport() per spec for responsive cases; presets ≠ real devices (9.17).
- Headless Chrome ≠ headed Chrome for a few CSS/video bugs — reproduce with --headed before blaming Cypress.
- Playwright: --headed / devices project. Selenium: ChromeOptions headless.
chapters.contentMarkdown:
## The three ways you see a browser

```bash
npx cypress open                 # Cypress App + visible browser (UI Mode, 9.11)
npx cypress run                  # headless, CI default
npx cypress run --headed         # visible browser, no App sidebar, still "run" semantics (videos, retries runMode)
```

CI should call `cypress run` (or `cypress-io/github-action`, which does). `cypress open` on a runner is wrong (no display, or a stuck GUI).

Electron vs Chrome: `cypress run` without `--browser` uses Electron. If you develop in Chrome and CI uses Electron, you will "see" differences. Pin `--browser chrome` in CI to match.

## Viewport is config, then command

```js
export default defineConfig({
  viewportWidth: 1280,
  viewportHeight: 720,
});

cy.viewport(390, 844);
cy.viewport('iphone-x');
```

If your laptop App is stretched to 1800px, you are not running the same test as CI. Reproduce CI with `npx cypress run --headed --browser chrome` at the config viewport.

Device presets change **size** (and sometimes user-agent in some tools — in Cypress, treat it as size). They do not load WebKit (9.9).

## Headless quirks worth knowing

- Headless Chrome is close to headed Chromium; remaining gaps are usually video codecs, focus, or `window.screen`.
- Firefox headed vs headless can differ more than Chrome.
- `video: true` (11.8) costs CPU in headless CI — a flake source if the runner is tiny (12.4).

## Versus Playwright and Selenium

Playwright: `headless: true` default in CI; `devices['iPhone 13']` sets viewport **and** user-agent; WebKit still available. Selenium 4: `--headless=new`. Cypress: be explicit about browser name + viewport numbers.

Interview line: "`cypress run` is headless CI; `--headed` is not UI Mode. I pin viewport in config. `iphone-x` is a size, not a phone."
